summary: service options: arguments (ignored on systemd), enabled at boot, name, pattern for ps-based status, OpenRC runlevel, sleep between restart steps, and state (started, stopped, restarted, reloaded).
questions: How do I enable a service at boot without starting it?
What's the difference between restarted and reloaded?
How do I manage a service with a broken status command?
Why does reloaded start my stopped service?

answer_card.title: service parameters
answer_card.answer_md:
- `name` (required); need at least one of `state`/`enabled`
- `state`: `started`/`stopped` (idempotent), `restarted` (always), `reloaded` (always; starts if stopped)
- `enabled`: start on boot
- `pattern`: ps substring for status (not systemd)
- `sleep`: seconds between stop/start on restart (not systemd)
- `arguments` (alias `args`), `runlevel` (OpenRC) — ignored on systemd
